title: Bounded antecedent audit partially discharging the decision-sufficiency proposal's stop test
question: Does the existing Decision sufficiency on observation fibres proposal survive its declared stop test once the submitted antecedents on quotient factorisation, state abstraction, credal decisions and stability radii are checked directly?
summary: Audit whether the proposed general framework is substantially anticipated by established results in lumpability, aggregation, statistical sufficiency, state abstraction, robust decision theory and stability analysis. If so, close or reframe the programme as a bounded cross-field translation centred on any remaining Pearl-Manski junction.
whyNow: The existing proposal explicitly treats framework duplication as a stopping risk and records its prior-art search as not started. The submitted issue supplies named, section-level antecedents and a one-day reading gate, while also declaring unread sources and self-audit bias.

atlasAnchors.basis: The proposed framework begins by separating identification from later estimation or optimisation.
Its decision question ranges over observationally admissible states rather than a single identified parameter.
The submitted antecedent audit directly queries whether stability-radius results already supply the proposed margin concept.
This release supplies the fibre-constancy statement and cites part of the antecedent literature under audit.

cheapFalsifier: Read Li, Walsh and Littman (2006), Ruggeri and Sivaganesan (2000), and Sotskov, Tanaev and Werner (1998) at the cited definitions and sections. If the four licence questions map to the state-abstraction hierarchy and the proposed margin maps to the established stability radius, close the general-framework route and retain only any independently supported junction claim.
expectedInformationGain: The audit should distinguish an already-established framework, a useful but non-novel translation across fields, and a narrower unresolved junction that could justify further work without overclaiming priority.

resourceEstimate.basis: The proposed first gate is a bounded direct reading of three named sources, expected to take less than one day.
